Patchset 3 took Verified -1 on a different, smaller failure: tests/scripts/test_reconciler_core_seam_clean_heldout.py::test_read_via_markers_are_bounded_and_confined, {'_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py': (0, 1)}. The module-size gate was fixed by the split. Not environmental; no recheck. Patchset 4 fixes it plus both LLM-Review advisories.

BUDGET REGISTRY — it lives in the test file itself, not a separate registry: _OWNED_FILES (line 47), _MARKER_BUDGET (line 88) and _TOTAL_MARKER_CAP in tests/scripts/test_reconciler_core_seam_clean_heldout.py, the RP-04 C3a-CORE seam-clean proof. My extraction carried the REBAR_RECONCILER_LOCK_STEAL '# read-via:' marked line out of __main__.py together with _lock_steal_enabled, so __main__ held 0 against a budget of exactly 1. Fixed by updating the budget to reality, NOT by putting the line back (that would undo part of the split): _pass_lock_lifecycle.py added to _OWNED_FILES so it inherits __main__'s config-ownership rather than escaping the gate by being new, and the _MARKER_BUDGET entry moved with the line (__main__.py now budgets zero). _TOTAL_MARKER_CAP stays 6 deliberately — the line RELOCATED; no read was added and none blanket-marked. The 'exactly' assertion is untouched. Verified RED->GREEN locally: with the stale budget restored the test fails ('unexpected markers in: _pass_lock_lifecycle.py'); with the fix, 10 passed.

ADVISORY 1 (correctness, and the right call) — R3's sanctioned entry set was keyed on rel.stem, so ANY file in src/ or scripts/ named git_adapter.py / _ref_lock.py / _ref_lock_push.py was exempt regardless of package. For a gate whose entire value is precision that is opt-out-by-filename. Now keyed on the EXACT repo-relative path (SEAM_INTERNAL_FILES, built from src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler). The receiver binding stays name-based on purpose and the header now states why: in the binding a module's name is EVIDENCE that a call is a git call; in the exemption the name would be a CLAIM of trust, which has to be earned by residency. A parametrized regression test pins it — a lookalike of each of the three seam files under another package still fires. Note this changed the pre-existing seam tests from RED to GREEN in the right direction: they had been passing against synthetic src/rebar/git_adapter.py paths, which is exactly the bypass.

ADVISORY 2 (tests) — R3's dotted-attribute receiver branch (receiver is an attribute chain, binding read off its TRAILING name) now has both halves covered: rebar_reconciler.git_adapter.add/commit fires; pkg.sub.session_store.add/commit does not.

SCOPE: all three fixes are confined to scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py and two test files. Nothing reaches into shipped src/rebar behavior beyond the already-authorized split, so no re-partitioning is needed.

Gates on patchset 4: make lint exit 0 (complexity active=49 new=0 increased=0), make typecheck exit 0 over 569 files, check_raw_git_writes.py exit 0, 3010 tests passed across the lint tests + seam-clean proof + tests/unit/rebar_reconciler. test_raw_git_write_lint.py is now 54 tests (was 42 pre-change). origin/main advanced by 12 commits (incl. 1918, 1920) with ZERO file overlap with this change, so Gerrit's Rebase-If-Necessary handles it server-side and I did not pre-rebase. Pushed as patchset 4 (commit a2115dcd83); both votes re-running.
